transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO - NovaSprint), Aisha Khan (Lead ML Eng), Tom Reyes (DevOps)
---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros then we'll get into what you're trying to build and the TTFT goals.
[00:12] Carlos: Hey thanks, uh yeah I can start. I'm Carlos, CTO at NovaSprint. We're building a realtime summarization & routing layer for delivery ops, needs low latency.
[00:23] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here, ML lead. We're prototyping a lambda-style microservice that hits an inference endpoint for summaries and embeddings. Primary concerns: latency and data privacy.
[00:36] Tom: Tom, ops, curious about the VPC and keys flow, like how our KMS would talk to Redwood.
[00:44] Jordan: Awesome. Priya, want to cover the quickstart and hosting options?
[00:48] Priya (Redwood SE): Sure—so Redwood has three common paths: Hosted API (self-serve, fastest TTFT), Dedicated (reserved capacity with predictable throughput), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For quick protos we usually recommend self-serve hosted with free credits so you can get to first token in hours.
[01:12] Aisha: When you say hours, does that include schemaed outputs, streaming, and our custom prompt templates?
[01:19] Priya: Yeah, for a simple integration — calling the text generation or embeddings endpoint, basic streaming — teams often hit first token within 30–90 minutes if they have an API key and sample prompts. If you want VPC connectivity or SSO tied in, that adds days-weeks.
[01:36] Carlos: Okay. Our timeline for a customer-facing beta is 8 weeks. We need an answer on whether hosted will pass compliance for us or we need Private.
[01:45] Jordan: Understood. What compliance controls do you need? SOC2? Data residency?
[01:49] Aisha: SOC2 is required. Also need audit logs, KMS integration ideally. 
[01:56] Tom: And we'd like to avoid sending PII to any shared model if possible — or at least know the retention and encryption.
[02:05] Priya: We support SOC2-compliant hosted environments; we also offer Private with a customer-managed control plane for full isolation. Hosted can be good if you restrict retention and enable our data encryption-at-rest and in-transit plus optional request-level redaction. Note: hosted in multi-tenant infra is not air-gapped.
[02:28] Speaker 4 (mislabeled): Right — dedicated reserved capacity gives you predictable latency because you own the GPU pools. There's a cost uplift vs hosted pay-as-you-go.
[02:40] Carlos: Can you ballpark that uplift? We need cost per 1M tokens as naive baseline then dedicate uplift.
[02:48] Jordan: Ballpark — depends on model and quantization — but Dedicated is often 2–4x cheaper at scale vs hosted on a per-token basis if you're committing to reserved capacity. For small pilots, hosted credits are cheaper because no commit.
[03:05] Aisha: And private? If we go VPC, is there an ops burden on our side?
[03:11] Priya: For VPC we offer a private control plane with integrations to your KMS/HSM. There's some network setup (VPC peering or PrivateLink), but we manage the control plane. On-prem is heavier — we ship a package and integrate with your infra.
[03:28] Tom: If we do VPC can we keep model weights in Redwood or do they have to be pulled into our VPC?
[03:34] Priya: Model weights remain on Redwood side for VPC deployments; traffic endpoints and the control plane are private. On-prem option is where weights run inside your network.
[03:43] Carlos: For TTFT, if we try hosted first with credits, and then move to Dedicated later, how seamless is that?
[03:50] Jordan: Seamless in terms of API — same endpoints, same SDK. You can pin model versions and use rollout policies. Priya can talk about KV cache and batching differences when you move.
[04:00] Priya: Yep — moving to Dedicated usually requires a config change to route traffic to your reserved pool; some tuning on batch sizes and max tokens helps. KV cache semantics are preserved but you may want different cache sizing.
[04:12] Aisha: You mentioned KV cache — our pipelines use long context and we often re-use prefixes. How does caching work across tenants?
[04:20] Priya: Cache is per-customer on Dedicated/Private; on hosted it's multi-tenant but logically separated — prefix caching can be effective but for strict isolation Dedicated or VPC is recommended.
[04:31] Carlos: Ok, that helps. On the free credits, what's the usual amount and how long do they last?
[04:36] Jordan: We typically give new signups a one-time credit bundle geared to reach a few hundred thousand tokens — enough for proofs-of-concept. For pilots we can arrange extra credits with an AE. Credits generally expire in 90 days, but we can extend for pilot timelines.
[04:55] Tom: Any limits on QPS or concurrency for the free tier?
[04:58] Priya: There's rate limiting by default but you can request temporary increases for benchmark windows. For high-concurrency tests we recommend scheduling a benchmark with the SE team.
[05:09] Speaker 1 (Jordan): Aisha, if we ran a benchmark what are your targets — p95 latency, throughput, tokens per request?
[05:15] Aisha: Ideally p95 < 300ms for summaries of ~300 tokens, throughput ~150 requests/s for the service under load. Those are ambitious but it's our goal.
[05:25] Priya: We'll need your prompt set and payload sizes. For p95 at that scale we may recommend a smaller model or quantized variants, plus batching and prefix caching. We'll test hosted first then show Dedicated numbers.
[05:38] Carlos: What about model fallbacks? If a model version regresses in quality, can we automatically fallback to a prior artifact?
[05:45] Priya: Yes, we have rollouts and automatic fallback policies. You can pin a version and control canaries, AB tests. Also we're integrating eval hooks tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions.
[05:59] Tom: On security again — KMS: does Redwood call our KMS or do we push keys? How's key wrapping handled?
[06:06] Priya: For VPC/private we can integrate with your cloud KMS via a service account; we can also support customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption. For on-prem there's HSM support and key wrapping patterns. We'll map this in the checklist.
[06:21] Aisha: Any special network egress policies? We need to restrict outbound to our internal logging and to Redwood only.
[06:27] Priya: You can restrict via VPC firewall rules and PrivateLink. For hosted self-serve, IP allowlisting is limited — VPC is the best fit for strict network controls.
[06:39] Carlos: If we start with hosted, what's the minimum work to integrate SSO for our internal dashboards?
[06:45] Jordan: For SSO it's a few days — SAML or OIDC. That can be part of the pilot scope; it doesn't block getting to first token.
[06:53] Aisha: Ok cool. Could you outline a suggested timeline: hosted quickstart to prototype in one week, then benchmark and decision to Dedicated or VPC in three weeks?
[07:03] Priya: Yes, suggested plan: Day 0–2: sign up, claim credits, integrate basic API calls. Day 3–7: iterate prompts, test streaming and embeddings. Week 2: schedule benchmark with SE for rate/latency. Week 3–4: decide on Dedicated reservation or VPC setup.
[07:20] Jordan: I'll include that in a playbook we send.
[07:23] Carlos: How are logs and audit trails surfaced? We need per-request IDs and token-level cost accounting.
[07:29] Priya: Console exposes per-route and per-token breakdowns, trace hooks, and exportable logs. For compliance, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM in Private deployments.
[07:41] Tom: Good. For telemetry, we need sample IDs to link traces to our upstream requests — is there a correlation ID?
[07:47] Priya: Yes we surface request IDs and you can pass in headers; we also have tracing hooks that you can wire into your tracing system.
[07:56] Aisha: About quantization — if we pick a quantized model to improve latency, does that hit quality for our summarization?
[08:02] Priya: Depends on the model and prompt; we'll do A/B comparison as part of the benchmark. Our Optimize team provides quantization recommendations per workload.
[08:13] Carlos: Any surprises around tokenization differences or cost accounting? Sometimes different SDKs count tokens differently.
[08:19] Jordan: We publish how tokens are counted per model and SDK. We'll include a quick note about tokenization differences, and our console shows token counts per request.
[08:28] Speaker 2 (Aisha): Ok, let's talk obstacles — our infra team is worried about provisioning new keys and opening PrivateLink within the quarter. If that's a blocker, I'd rather start hosted and push sensitive workloads later.
[08:41] Priya: That's a common pattern. Start hosted for product validation, move to VPC for compliance-sensitive traffic during pilot-to-prod.
[08:50] Carlos: Cool. On the commercial side—if we do Dedicated, what's the typical contract length and SLAs?
[08:56] Jordan: Dedicated often comes with 12-month reserved commitments and SLA targets for uptime and latency tiers. We'll share more flexible pilot contracts for early customers.
[09:06] Tom: Can pilot usage roll into reserved commitment credit? E.g., credit we use in pilot counts toward initial commitment?
[09:12] Jordan: Yes, we often apply pilot credits toward a first commitment if you convert within the pilot window. We'll detail that in the commercial note.
[09:20] Aisha: Ok that's motivating. One more technical: for our request volume pattern we have spikes — can Dedicated autoscale?
[09:27] Priya: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity. We can configure autoscale thresholds to keep p95 latency within SLO.
[09:36] Carlos: Perfect. Let's cover the benchmark scope — Aisha, you wanted p95 <300ms at 150rps for 300 token summaries — anything to add?
[09:44] Aisha: Also measure throughput at 95k tokens/min and look at error rates when we hit cache miss scenarios.
[09:51] Priya: We'll include cache warmup tests and compare hosted vs dedicated. For Hosted we'll show baseline and then show Dedicated improvements.
[10:00] Jordan: Quick clarifying Q — do you need embeddings in the same flow or separate endpoint?
[10:04] Aisha: Separate, but both will be used. Embeddings for similarity search in routing.
[10:09] Priya: Great — we'll plan a two-part benchmark: generation latency and embeddings throughput.
[10:15] Carlos: Any docs you can send now? Security whitepaper, VPC checklist, quickstart playbook?
[10:20] Jordan: We'll send a link pack: quickstart repo, SE benchmark template, SOC2 and network checklist.
[10:26] Tom: For the repo, do you have example infra as code for VPC peering?
[10:30] Priya: Yes — we'll include CloudFormation/Terraform snippets for PrivateLink and VPC setup.
[10:36] Speaker 1 (Jordan): Alright let's go to a quick Q&A before wrapping.
[10:40] Aisha: Does Redwood store training data or fine-tune models with our data by default? We want to opt out.
[10:46] Priya: By default we don't train on customer data. For hosted you can opt out of data usage for training, and for Private it's fully customer controlled. We'll put that in the security doc too.
[10:57] Carlos: Great. Anything else we missed?
[11:00] Tom: Just the timeline confirmation.
[11:03] Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan to send credits/playbook, Priya to send VPC/KMS checklist and schedule benchmark window, Aisha to provide prompts and targets. We'll set a follow-up in a week to confirm.
[11:15] Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:18] Carlos: Thanks, bye.
---
Post-call notes (auto):
